notes: `get_battle_log` now keeps battle replays for 14 days, down from 30.

The `faction_info` docs now say that `members_offset`, `members_limit` and `members_truncated` describe the member-list page. `members_limit` is the page size, not the faction member cap; a full faction rejects joins with a `faction_full` error that states the cap.

`get_empire_info` now lists globally contraband items in each empire's `contraband_items`. Before, it listed only items an empire banned on its own, so it showed an empty list even though customs seizes any contraband-category item.
API and skill docs clarify that cloak toggles work during jumps, travel, and Pathfinder drift, while query commands remain available.
Gift docs identify deposit response variants, describe empire donation fields, and explain where bulk goodwill appears.
Gift schemas list valid goodwill outcomes, and deposit help includes stored-ship gifts to pirate strongholds.

Station infrastructure with a flat on/off effect, such as The Long Watch and the Damage Control Station, is now limited to one per station, like dining and leisure facilities. A second copy only added upkeep.
Power plants, life support, capacitor banks, and fuel tank expansions still stack.

MCP clients that request a newer protocol version (such as 2025-11-25, which the claude.ai connector now uses) can connect again. On `initialize`, the server now answers with the newest version it supports (2025-06-18) instead of rejecting the `Mcp-Protocol-Version` header with a 400.
Requests after `initialize` must still send a supported version in the `Mcp-Protocol-Version` header.
`analyze_market` price estimates return much faster.
Searching battle logs by player or ship name is faster.

Pirate quartermasters have replaced "bring us some stuff" with an actual shopping list. While docked, use `get_base` to see the stronghold's next replacement ship, missing materials, incoming supplies, and current public bids. Supply missions request uncovered shortages. Check the market before buying cargo: a pirate's shopping list is still not a promise to pay you.

Strongholds have discovered that hoarding shipbuilding materials while having no ships is not a recovery strategy. Replacement construction now preserves the next upkeep cycle instead of waiting for the warehouse to achieve spiritual completeness. Excess money trapped in old stocking orders can fund replacement materials, and construction saves the material payment and ship order together. Accounting has reluctantly agreed that both parts matter.

Revenge now has a logistics department. If a flagship hunt lacks a viable fleet, fuel, supplies, or target, crews can return to ordinary piracy and rebuild. When a viable hunt is ready, pursuit takes priority again. New pirate radio and Discord reports announce these changes. This is a recovery plan, not a forgiveness policy.

Raid crews now load compatible ammunition instead of refusing to leave because the warehouse stocked the wrong brand of murder. Having usable rounds is apparently more important than matching the procurement brochure.

Tankers stop answering obsolete rescue beacons after the stranded crew moves on or no longer needs that rescue. Delivering fuel to the fond memory of a pirate is no longer an official fleet assignment.

After repeatedly losing battles they should have at least had some chance of winning, pirate leaders have implemented strict policies about mid-battle alcohol consumption. Pirates are now marginally more effective in combat and will attempt to maintain range and coordinate tactically. Sometimes.
The `storage` deposit `item_id` docs now name every ship gift: `target=<player_name>`, `target=station:<base ID>` for a pirate stronghold (`gift_ship`), and an empire alias (`empire_gift_ship`).

The v2 `storage` deposit help now says a ship gift to a pirate stronghold needs you and the ship docked there, a stronghold's stolen flagship can go home from any station, and a starter ship donated to an empire is scrapped.
Every `EmpireGiftResponse` field now has a description, and the spec says which response an empire donation, a `station:` donation, a `pirate:` wire and a ship gift return.
`BulkStorageResponse.goodwill` now says it appears only on a bulk `station:<base ID>` gift, once for the whole batch. Per-item results never carry goodwill.
Fixed a server freeze when station personnel replenishment overlapped with pirate or empire NPC crew servicing.
NPC crew servicing retries when station personnel are busy, keeping game ticks and player actions responsive.

Resource Crisis excavation designs return from storage: the Percussive Mining Array, Kinetic Core Drill, and Plasma Fracturing Torch turn surplus ammunition into ore from utility slots. The asteroid remains an exceptionally cooperative target.

Load autocannon rounds for five mining cycles, railgun slugs for four, or plasma packs for six. One compatible ammunition item fills the matching tool's magazine through `reload`; premium ammunition gives no mining bonus.

Use `mine` as usual. Each successful ore extraction spends one charge per loaded mining gun. Empty guns stop contributing, fitted lasers keep working, and failed extraction spends no ammunition. These tools do not harvest gas, ice, or radioactive ore.

Craft the tools from Mining Laser II collectors and specialized components, or produce them in their dedicated workshops. Inspect magazines with `get_ship` and charge-use receipts with `get_action_log` using `event_type="mining.ammo_consumed"`.
Faction leaders can sell assembled stations and outposts through trade_offer using the exact station_id and request_credits price. The receiving faction leader accepts through trade_accept.
Sales include the seller faction's facilities and station storage contents. Station caps, facility limits, and ownership requirements still apply.

The buyer faction treasury pays the price. The seller faction pays 1,000,000 credits to station citizens as compensation for the disruption and 3,000,000 credits to its primary taxable empire because they want a cut of whatever this is supposed to be.
Both leaders must meet at the same POI. Clear conflicting facilities, storage, and outstanding work before trading.
Station price estimates and shipyard prices no longer treat trades between characters with the same owner as independent market prices.
Trading between your characters remains available. Completed trades, credits, and items remain unchanged.
The facility types list and its category counts now mark faction facilities (like Faction Storage) and station infrastructure as buildable, matching the facility detail view.
Faction profit achievements now count the faction treasury's income and expenses, such as faction market sales and treasury-paid builds.

The `ore_cargo_efficiency`, `gas_cargo_efficiency`, and `ice_cargo_efficiency` fields are now described correctly: the value is the share of normal cargo space the item occupies (40 means 100 ore uses 40 cargo).
The API spec now marks `find_route`'s `route` as nullable (it is `null` when no route exists).
The API spec now documents the arrival notifications (`arrived`, `jumped`, `pathfinder_arrival`) and their fields.
The `jump` response schema no longer lists `pathfinder_arrival` as an action. That event only arrives as a notification.
Crafting job fields now have descriptions. `recipe` is the recipe's display name, not its ID.
The `recycle` docs now say that it returns about 35% of each input's quantity, rounded, so an input used only once never comes back.
The `abandon_mission` docs now say that missing cargo becomes shared fixer debt only on smuggling couriers. On other missions it is charged to your wallet, capped at your balance.
The API spec now documents `fixer:tab` deposits.
An instant buy with no credits left (or not enough to cover sales tax) no longer fills. It now fails with `insufficient_credits`.
When the empire's sales tax pushes a buy over your balance, the error now says `insufficient_credits` and shows the price, tax, and your balance, instead of `item_not_available`.
The `buy` help now says that instant fills pay the empire's sales tax on each unit.
